newDescription:
In this Year 3 English lesson, pupils learn how prepositions tell us about place, time and cause, and how the same preposition can sometimes have different functions depending on the sentence.

This lesson includes:
✔ Identifying prepositions that describe where something is
✔ Using place prepositions such as under, on, in, beside, beneath, behind, through and next to
✔ Understanding that a preposition can be a single word or a phrase
✔ Recognising prepositions of time, including at, during and on
✔ Recognising prepositions and prepositional phrases that explain cause, such as due to and because of
✔ Sorting prepositions into place, time and cause
✔ Understanding that some prepositions can belong to more than one group depending on how they are used

Pupils begin with a picture-based activity describing where escaped pets are hiding in a classroom. This introduces prepositions of place naturally through full sentences.

The lesson then develops the idea that prepositions can be words or phrases and can describe place, time or cause. Pupils examine examples such as on, next to, at, during and due to, before applying the ideas independently.

The final sorting activity asks pupils to classify prepositions into time, place and cause and to notice that words such as on and at can have more than one function depending on context.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to identify and use prepositions of place, time and cause and explain their function within a sentence.
